svg.text: Cold chain and coverage: two ways a vaccine fails
A vaccine given is not the same as a vaccine that worked
The cold chain
Store between +2 and +8 degrees Celsius
Read and record the fridge temperature twice daily
Vaccines in the body of the fridge, never the door
Ice packs conditioned until they sweat before packing
Freezing destroys the diluent-based vaccines
as surely as heat destroys the live ones
Too cold is a real error, not a safe margin
The vial monitor tells you the truth
Inner square lighter than the ring:
use this vial
Inner square as dark as the ring, or darker:
discard it, whatever the expiry date says
The monitor records heat over time; the date does not
Measuring coverage honestly
Numerator: children in the district who received the dose
Denominator: all children of that age who live there
Coverage above one hundred per cent usually means
the denominator is wrong, not that everyone came
Children crossing from a neighbouring district inflate it
An out-of-date population estimate does the same
Compare the first dose with the last: the gap between
them is the dropout, and that is the real problem
Why children are missed
Nobody followed up the defaulter from the register
The mother was turned away because the session was full
A child with a mild cold was sent home unnecessarily
The family moved, or works on a distant farm
A rumour spread and nobody answered it
Every one of these is a service failure,
not a refusal by the mother
Find the defaulters in the register before blaming the community
